reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes purchasing EasyBlock shares as a low-cost way to obtain recurring StrongBlock node income, presents a 30% return claim, demonstrates funding and buying shares, and urges viewers to enter sooner rather than later. It reinforces participation with compounding-income projections and links while presenting the return calculations and monthly-versus-daily earnings inconsistently, rather than merely reporting on or criticizing the offer.

citations.quote: buy EazyBlock shares which are $10 each and put that into the pot and then get rewarded with the 30% APR that the strong nodes generate
30% reward per month for strong nodes
So it's definitely worth getting in sooner rather than later, I'd say.
we can now purchase some additional shares on EasyBlock
you can see it just keeps going up and up and up and will keep compounding the interest that we get into new shares

opening.argument: The presentation is conditional commentary, not a promise of guaranteed earnings. The speaker expressly identifies EasyBlock as new and says its future still has to be observed, while tying the stated yield to StrongBlock's price remaining unchanged. The closing screen also labels the material “NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE.” Those qualifications matter: the speaker presents a possible outcome, acknowledges uncertainty, and leaves the investment decision to viewers rather than certifying safety or certainty.

citations.quote: Like I said it's a brand new system So we'll have to just see how it takes off
So as long as strong- the strong prices doesn't change you'll be earning the same yield of 30% per month

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited purchase instructions and yield discussion establish that the video discusses an investment, but they do not establish a guaranteed result or conceal the speaker's uncertainty. “Worth getting in sooner” is advocacy, yet it remains a personal assessment in a presentation that also calls the system brand new and conditions the yield on StrongBlock's price. The evidence therefore supports investment commentary with risk caveats, not necessarily deceptive certification.

citations.quote: Like I said it's a brand new system So we'll have to just see how it takes off
So as long as strong- the strong prices doesn't change you'll be earning the same yield of 30% per month
So it's definitely worth getting in sooner rather than later, I'd say.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the video's operative message. The speaker still tells viewers that entering sooner is worthwhile and repeatedly models compounding income. “NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE” does not retract the solicitation, and the condition about StrongBlock's price merely qualifies the advertised yield; it does not explain the risks of the underlying scheme or establish that returns are actually achievable.

opening.argument: The video's dominant form is a practical walkthrough of how the technology and account operations work. It explains moving funds across networks, configuring MetaMask, swapping tokens, checking an explorer, and adding a custom token. The speaker demonstrates these steps with his own account and describes the system's mechanics, including how shares are represented and how funds move between networks. That is educational and operational content about a crypto tool, even though the presenter also offers an opinion about whether viewers may find it useful.

citations.quote: we're going to fill in these details
the reason you'll need to do this is because if you don't have USDC appearing in your list of assets here, then you need to add it in manually
So now I've clicked on that and this should update to say 23
I've purchased 10 nodes, spent $100

rebuttal.rebuttal: A tutorial can contain a product opinion without becoming a scam endorsement. The video spends substantial time showing wallet setup, transfers, token conversion, and transaction verification. Demonstrating how a user can interact with a protocol is consistent with technology education; the fact that the presenter completed a personal purchase shows the demonstration is concrete, not that viewers were promised an outcome.

citations.quote: I do recommend sending the minimum first just to make sure that it goes through okay
you can actually view the transaction that's happening
The first time you do this you will have to approve it in your MetaMask

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational walkthrough is precisely what makes the promotion actionable. The speaker does not merely explain wallet technology: he converts funds, buys shares, calculates expected income, and invites viewers to copy the process. Technical instructions therefore serve the EasyBlock offer, while the demonstration does not show that the advertised returns are valid or sustainable.

citations.quote: I'm going to put some USDT in my binance account here
we can now purchase some additional shares on EasyBlock
whether you're interested in actually investing in it yourself

opening.argument: The evidence is compatible with promotion of an ordinary paid service or access product, not proof of a scam mechanism. EasyBlock is described as selling shares for a stated price and pooling funds to acquire StrongBlock nodes. The video does not show a request for passwords, private keys, identity documents, or recruitment of a downline. It also demonstrates ordinary exchange and wallet operations, including a test transfer and transaction review. Promotion of a third-party service should not by itself be treated as proof that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: buy EazyBlock shares which are $10 each and put that into the pot
I do recommend sending the minimum first just to make sure that it goes through okay
you can actually view the transaction that's happening
they even post screenshots of their nodes that they've purchased and also add in the ether scan transactions

rebuttal.rebuttal: The record shows a paid share product and claimed node-based rewards, but it does not show the classic indicators of credential theft or a recruitment chain. The speaker describes public transaction checking and a small test transfer, which are ordinary precautions when using a crypto service. Even an enthusiastic referral-style presentation does not establish that the underlying service is inherently fraudulent.

citations.quote: I do recommend sending the minimum first just to make sure that it goes through okay
they even post screenshots of their nodes that they've purchased and also add in the ether scan transactions so you can actually see that they are all legitimate

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not request credentials or use a downline. The relevant mechanism shown is paid participation in a pool represented as producing recurring node returns. The speaker tells viewers to buy shares, supplies compounding projections, and encourages investment. Transaction visibility can show transfers occurred, but it does not prove that the promised returns, node ownership, or payout model are genuine.
